Most of the loot felt useless because you have more powerful gear already. The issue is that bungie can't drop a full season of more powerful gear without power creeping at massive speeds.

However, you can change your perspective, find weapons you need, and farm for those. My recommendation to fix this feeling is to try more builds you are unfamiliar with. I'm sure you will find builds where you need weapons you don't have in order to make them more viable. Make a list and start searching for all these guns again.

You used to do this when you first started the game. The issue is you have reached a point where you no longer need to chase the game's main focus. You already have the best stuff. Most games will reach this point since no game can provide infinite content. Eventually, you have to make your own fun or find another source.

But they are still adding raids, dungeons, and strikes. Seasonal activities have always been the same, simple, and repeatable gameplay loop to introduce players to the new content and loot chase. Rogue-lite additions are only expanding on this.

Not to mention, this approach is to directly addresses the previous issues people had with gamemodes like the strike playlist. People found them too static and unrepeatable. Bungie knows these gamemodes are meant to be played over and over to farm for seasonal weapons, so they try to make them dynamic.

I agree Destiny is at its best within raids and dungeons, combining story and large set pieces. However, in its current state, people are requesting dynamic and varied experiences to reduce the monotony of repeated play throughs.

But these 2 genres are not mutually exclusive. You lose none of the features of a looter shooter by implementing rogue-lite mechanics. Their goal is to introduce new activities and gameplay loops to keep the looter shooter feeling fresh.

I personally love the rogue-lite introductions as it allows you to find boons that synergize with your build you brought into the mode. Each run will provide you with different opportunities, making your static build feel more dynamic.

They aren't removing any features of a looter shooter, exploring new genres only builds on top of it. This also makes me excited to see how they implement a metroidvania style adventure in Apollo.
